source_refs.note: Practice MCQs written from Chapter 14 (PDF 305-322, printed 305-322); not printed in the book. Based on the chapter's text, tables, boxes and worked examples (numericals with changed values); none repeats the chapter exercise. Drafts needing academic review.

blocks.text: Practice MCQs for the whole of Chapter 14 (Atmosphere), arranged by the chapter's sections. Each question has one correct answer with a short explanation; numerical questions show the working.
Introduction: major, minor and trace components

blocks.prompt: 1 The major components of the atmosphere are:
blocks.explanation: Major components are nitrogen (about 78%) and oxygen (about 21%) (Introduction).

book_ref.quote: Major components are nitrogen (78.00%) and oxygen (21.01%)

blocks.prompt: 2 Argon (0.93%) and carbon dioxide (0.04%) are classed as which components of the atmosphere?
blocks.explanation: Argon and carbon dioxide are the minor components (Introduction).

book_ref.quote: Minor components are argon (0.93%), carbon dioxide (0.04%)

blocks.prompt: 3 Which of the following is a trace component of the atmosphere?
blocks.explanation: Trace components are methane, hydrogen, neon, helium, krypton and xenon (Introduction).

book_ref.quote: Trace components are methane, hydrogen, neon, helium, krypton, and xenon.

blocks.prompt: 4 Using the chapter's percentages, nitrogen and oxygen together make up about what percentage of the atmosphere?

book_ref.quote: The atmosphere is a sphere of different gases around the earth.

blocks.prompt: 5 The four layers of the atmosphere are distinguished on the basis of:

options.text: the change in temperature with increasing altitude

blocks.explanation: The layers are determined by the change in temperature observed with increasing altitude (14.1).

book_ref.quote: determined by the change in temperature that is observed with increasing altitude

blocks.prompt: 6 The troposphere extends from the ground up to about:
blocks.explanation: The troposphere is the lowest region and extends up to 12 km (14.1 i).

book_ref.quote: It is the lowest region of the atmosphere which extends up to 12 km.

blocks.prompt: 7 The densest layer of the atmosphere, in which rain, lightning and hurricanes occur, is the:
blocks.explanation: The troposphere is the densest layer and major weather events occur in it (14.1 i).

book_ref.quote: It is the densest layer of the atmosphere.

blocks.prompt: 8 In the troposphere the temperature falls from 17 °C to -58 °C over 12 km. What is the average fall in temperature per kilometre?

book_ref.quote: In this region, temperature decreases from 17 °C to -58 °C regularly.

blocks.prompt: 9 The stratosphere lies at a height of:
blocks.explanation: The stratosphere lies 12-50 km above the earth's surface (14.1 ii).

book_ref.quote: at a distance of 12-50 km above the earth surface

blocks.prompt: 10 In the stratosphere, temperature:
blocks.explanation: In the stratosphere the temperature increases from -58 °C to -2 °C (14.1 ii).

book_ref.quote: Temperature increases from -58 °C to -2 °C.

blocks.prompt: 11 In the upper stratosphere, ozone absorbs high-energy UV radiation and breaks down into:
blocks.explanation: O₃(g) → O₂(g) + O(g) in the presence of UV light (hν) (14.1 ii).

book_ref.quote: Since ozone in the upper layer absorbs high energy ultraviolet radiations from the Sun.

blocks.prompt: 12 In the middle stratosphere the reaction O₂(g) + O(g) → O₃(g) is:
blocks.explanation: Monoatomic and diatomic oxygen recombine to form ozone in an exothermic reaction; this forms the ozone layer (14.1 ii).

book_ref.quote: monoatomic oxygen and diatomic oxygen recombine to form ozone which is an exothermic reaction

blocks.prompt: 13 According to the chapter, ozone is not formed in the lower stratosphere because:

options.text: there is no diatomic oxygen there
all the ozone is destroyed by rain
very little UV reaches it, so monoatomic oxygen is not found there

blocks.explanation: The lower stratosphere receives very low UV, so monoatomic oxygen is absent and ozone is not formed (14.1 ii).

book_ref.quote: The lower stratosphere receives very low ultraviolet radiations

blocks.prompt: 14 The coldest region of the atmosphere is found in the:
blocks.explanation: In the mesosphere temperature falls to -93 °C; the coldest region is in this layer (14.1 iii).

book_ref.quote: The coldest region of the atmosphere is located in this layer.

blocks.prompt: 15 The mesosphere extends from about:
blocks.explanation: The mesosphere extends to about 50-85 km from the ground (14.1 iii).

book_ref.quote: It extends to a height of about 50 – 85 km from the ground.

blocks.prompt: 16 The temperature in the thermosphere rises with altitude because of:

options.text: absorption of energetic UV and X-rays

blocks.explanation: The rise is caused by absorption of energetic UV and X-rays (14.1 iv).

book_ref.quote: The increase in the temperature is caused due to the absorption of energetic ultra-violet (UV) and X-rays.

blocks.prompt: 17 The temperature in the upper thermosphere can range from:
blocks.explanation: Upper thermosphere temperatures range from 500 °C to 2000 °C or higher (14.1 iv).

book_ref.quote: Temperature in the upper thermosphere can range from 500 °C to 2000 °C or higher.

blocks.prompt: 18 In which two layers does the temperature increase with increasing altitude?
blocks.explanation: Temperature rises from -58 °C to -2 °C in the stratosphere and rises with altitude in the thermosphere (85-600 km) (14.1).

book_ref.quote: It extends from 85 km to 600 km above the earth surface.

blocks.prompt: 19 Pollutants are best described as:

options.text: gases, liquids and solids that are harmful to the environment
only gases that are harmful to the environment
substances that make up the major part of air
only solid particles in the air

blocks.explanation: Pollutants are substances (gases, liquids and solids) harmful to the environment (14.2).

book_ref.quote: Pollutants are substances (gases, liquids and solids) that are harmful to the environment.

blocks.prompt: 20 Carbon monoxide from a motor vehicle exhaust is an example of a:
blocks.explanation: Primary pollutants are directly produced or emitted, such as CO from vehicle exhaust (14.2).

book_ref.quote: Primary pollutants are substances directly produced or emitted

blocks.prompt: 21 Secondary pollutants are formed by:
blocks.explanation: Secondary pollutants are formed by chemical reactions of primary pollutants (14.2).

book_ref.quote: Secondary pollutants are formed due to chemical reactions of primary pollutants.

blocks.prompt: 22 The pollutants collectively known as NOₓ are:
blocks.explanation: Oxides of nitrogen NO and NO₂ are collectively known as NOₓ (14.2).

book_ref.quote: Oxides of Nitrogen (NO and NO₂) collectively known as NOₓ

blocks.prompt: 23 Which set lists the heavy metals named as air pollutants in the chapter?
blocks.explanation: Heavy metals listed as pollutants are Pb, Hg and Cd (14.2).

book_ref.quote: Heavy Metals (Pb, Hg and Cd)

blocks.prompt: 24 Which natural event produces significant quantities of NOₓ?
blocks.explanation: A thunderbolt produces significant quantities of oxides of nitrogen (14.3.1).

book_ref.quote: Thunderbolt produces significant quantities of oxides of nitrogen (NOₓ).

blocks.prompt: 25 According to the chapter, algae on the surface of the oceans give out:
blocks.explanation: Algae on the ocean surface give out H₂S (14.3.1).

book_ref.quote: algae on the surface of the oceans, which gives out hydrogen sulphide (H₂S)

blocks.prompt: 26 Swamps and other humid zones are a natural source of:
blocks.explanation: Humid zones such as swamps, peat bogs and shallow lakes produce methane (14.3.1).

book_ref.quote: humid zones such as swamps, peat-bags or little deep lakes, which produce methane (CH₄)

blocks.prompt: 27 Factories and electric power plants are examples of:
blocks.explanation: Human-made sources are mobile (cars, trucks, aeroplanes, marine engines) or point sources (factories, power plants) (14.3.2).

book_ref.quote: point sources (factories, electric power plants etc.)

blocks.prompt: 28 Which of the following is a mobile source of air pollution?
blocks.explanation: Mobile sources are cars, trucks, aeroplanes and marine engines (14.3.2).

book_ref.quote: Such sources can be classified as either mobile (cars, trucks, air planes, marine engines)

blocks.prompt: 29 Carbon monoxide is produced mainly by:

options.text: action of UV light on ozone

blocks.explanation: CO is produced mainly by incomplete combustion: 2C(s) + O₂(g) → 2CO(g) (14.4.1).

book_ref.quote: Carbon monoxide (CO) is produced mainly due to incomplete combustion of fossil fuels.

blocks.prompt: 30 Carbon monoxide is poisonous because it:

options.text: dissolves in rain to form an acid
binds haemoglobin more strongly than oxygen

blocks.explanation: CO binds blood haemoglobin more strongly than oxygen, excluding oxygen from respiration (14.4.1).

book_ref.quote: It binds blood hemoglobin more strongly than oxygen

blocks.prompt: 31 Carbon monoxide poisoning can be reversed by giving:
blocks.explanation: CO poisoning can be reversed by giving high pressure oxygen (14.4.1).

book_ref.quote: The CO poisonous can be reversed by giving high pressure oxygen.

blocks.prompt: 32 The key greenhouse gas emitted by human activities such as combustion of fossil fuels is:
blocks.explanation: CO₂ is the key greenhouse gas from human activities; it traps heat, leading to global warming (14.4.1).

book_ref.quote: Carbon dioxide (CO₂) is a primary greenhouse gas that traps heat in the atmosphere

blocks.prompt: 33 Nitrogen and oxygen combine to form nitric oxide, N₂(g) + O₂(g) → 2NO(g), under the condition of:
blocks.explanation: N₂ and O₂ form NO at high temperature (14.4.2).

book_ref.quote: NOₓ is produced as a result of the following chemical reactions:

blocks.prompt: 34 Nitric oxide reacts further with oxygen to give:
blocks.explanation: 2NO(g) + O₂ → 2NO₂ (nitrogen dioxide) (14.4.2).

book_ref.quote: It is generally produced from burning fossil fuels.

blocks.prompt: 35 A natural source of nitrous oxide (N₂O) is:

options.text: microbial processes in soil and oceans

blocks.explanation: Natural N₂O comes from microbial processes in soil and oceans where bacteria break down nitrogen compounds (14.4.2).

book_ref.quote: Natural sources of N₂O include microbial processes in soil and oceans

blocks.prompt: 36 A human activity that releases N₂O is:

options.text: use of synthetic fertilizers in agriculture

blocks.explanation: Human sources of N₂O include agricultural activities (synthetic fertilizers) and industrial combustion (14.4.2).

book_ref.quote: Human activities include agricultural activities (synthetic fertilizers)

blocks.prompt: 37 Oxides of sulphur (SOₓ) are emitted primarily by:
blocks.explanation: SO₂ and SO₃ are emitted primarily by burning coal and oil (14.4.3).

book_ref.quote: These gases are emitted primarily by burning coal and oil.

blocks.prompt: 38 The major source of acid deposition in the air is:
blocks.explanation: SO₂ is the major source of acid deposition (14.4.3).

book_ref.quote: SO₂ is the major source of acid deposition in the air.

blocks.prompt: 39 The most common hydrocarbon air pollutant is:
blocks.explanation: Methane is the most common hydrocarbon and air pollutant (14.4.4).

book_ref.quote: Methane is the most common hydrocarbon and air pollutant.

blocks.prompt: 40 The major source of hydrocarbon emission is:
blocks.explanation: Automobiles are the major source of hydrocarbon emission (14.4.4).

book_ref.quote: Automobiles are the major source of hydrocarbon emission.

blocks.prompt: 41 Low-altitude ozone harms rubber, fabric dyes and paints because it is a:
blocks.explanation: Ozone is a powerful oxidizing agent and harms humans, plants, rubber, fabric dyes and paints (14.4.5).

book_ref.quote: Ozone is a powerful oxidizing agent.

blocks.prompt: 42 The decrease in the concentration of ozone in the stratosphere is called:
blocks.explanation: The decrease in stratospheric ozone concentration is called depletion of ozone (14.4.6).

book_ref.quote: The decrease in the concentration of ozone in stratosphere is called depletion of ozone.

blocks.prompt: 43 At room temperature, chlorofluorocarbons exist as:
blocks.explanation: CFCs exist as gases or low-boiling liquids at room temperature (14.4.6).

book_ref.quote: These compounds exist as gases or low boiling liquids at room temperature

blocks.prompt: 44 In the stratosphere, UV radiation breaks a CFC molecule such as CFCl₃ to set free a:
blocks.explanation: CFCl₃ → CFCl₂ + Cl• under UV; the particle is a chlorine atom with an unpaired electron (the book's correction: not a chloride ion) (14.4.6).

book_ref.quote: where they are broken down by UV radiation creating chloride free radical (Cl•)

blocks.prompt: 45 In the reaction Cl• + O₃ → ClO• + O₂, the chlorine free radical:
blocks.explanation: Cl• attacks O₃, forming ClO• and O₂; Cl• is then set free again to break down another O₃ (14.4.6).

book_ref.quote: The formation of another chlorine free radical in the last step that can further break down another molecule of O₃.

blocks.prompt: 46 The balanced step that sets the chlorine free radical free again in the ozone-destroying cycle is:
blocks.explanation: The book's correction: the step is ClO• + O → Cl• + O₂ (the printed ClO• + O₂ → Cl• + O₂ is not balanced) (14.4.6).

book_ref.quote: The 2nd and the 3rd steps are repeated many times.

blocks.prompt: 47 If one CFC molecule can destroy up to 100,000 ozone molecules, up to how many ozone molecules can 25 CFC molecules destroy?

book_ref.quote: The decomposition of one molecule of CFCs can destroy up to 100,000 molecules of ozone.

blocks.prompt: 48 CFCs released at the ground destroy ozone after they:

options.text: diffuse into the stratosphere and are broken down by UV radiation
react with SO₂ in the troposphere

blocks.explanation: CFCs diffuse into the stratosphere, where UV radiation breaks them to give chlorine free radicals that destroy O₃ (14.4.6).

book_ref.quote: Chlorofluorocarbons are known to diffuse into the stratosphere

blocks.prompt: 49 Polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons (PAHs) are composed of:
blocks.explanation: PAHs are composed of fused multiple aromatic rings (14.4.7).

book_ref.quote: composed of fused multiple aromatic rings are common environmental pollutants

blocks.prompt: 50 Which of the following is an example of a PAH?
blocks.explanation: Naphthalene, anthracene and phenanthrene are examples of PAHs (14.4.7).

book_ref.quote: They are generated primarily during the incomplete combustion of fossil fuels

blocks.prompt: 51 PAHs are generated primarily during:
blocks.explanation: PAHs are generated primarily during incomplete combustion of coal, oil, petrol and wood, and even in grilled foods (14.4.7).

book_ref.quote: Some PAHs in the environment originate from the natural sources

blocks.prompt: 52 Persistent organic pollutants (POPs) are organic compounds that:

options.text: are broken down rapidly by sunlight
resist chemical, biological and photolytic degradation

blocks.explanation: POPs are resistant to degradation through chemical, biological and photolytic processes (14.4.8).

book_ref.quote: These are organic compounds that are resistant to degradation through chemical, biological and photolytic processes.

blocks.prompt: 53 According to Table 14.1, polychlorinated biphenyls (PCBs) are used in:

options.text: electrical equipment, inks, adhesives and paints

blocks.explanation: PCBs are used in electrical equipment, surface coating ink, adhesives and paints (Table 14.1).

book_ref.quote: Used in electrical equipment, surface coating ink, adhesives and paints

blocks.prompt: 54 The POP DDT (dichlorodiphenyltrichloroethane) is used as:
blocks.explanation: DDT is used as an insecticide in agriculture; its correct name is dichlorodiphenyltrichloroethane (Table 14.1, book correction).

book_ref.quote: Used as an insecticide in agriculture

blocks.prompt: 55 POPs can affect people and wildlife far from where they were released because they:

options.text: are destroyed at once by sunlight
remain only in the soil where they are used
persist and are carried by wind and water

blocks.explanation: POPs are persistent and travel by wind and water, so they affect people far away (14.4.8).

book_ref.quote: Most POPs are generated in one country can affect people and wildlife far from where they are used and released.

blocks.prompt: 56 Volatile organic compounds (VOCs) are organic compounds that:

options.text: are made of fused aromatic rings only

blocks.explanation: VOCs are a large group of organic compounds that easily evaporate at room temperature (14.4.9).

book_ref.quote: A large group of organic compounds that easily evaporates at room temperature.

blocks.prompt: 57 The major sources of VOCs that affect outdoor air quality are:
blocks.explanation: Liquid fuels are major sources of VOCs affecting outdoor air quality (14.4.9).

book_ref.quote: Liquid fuels are major sources of VOCs that impact outdoor air quality.

blocks.prompt: 58 A long-term effect of exposure to VOCs is:

options.text: damage to the liver, kidney and central nervous system

blocks.explanation: Short-term: eye, nose, throat irritation, headache, nausea; long-term: damage to liver, kidney and central nervous system (14.4.9).

book_ref.quote: damage to the liver, kidney and central nervous system are long term exposures

blocks.prompt: 59 Which of the following is a common VOC named in the chapter?
blocks.explanation: Common VOCs: benzene, xylene, toluene, ethanol, formaldehyde, acetone (14.4.9).

book_ref.quote: Some common VOCs are benzene, xylene, toluene, ethanol, formaldehyde and acetone

blocks.prompt: 60 Particulate matter (PM) refers to tiny substances floating in the air as:

options.text: solid particles, liquid droplets or both

blocks.explanation: PM is tiny substances floating in air as solid particles or liquid droplets or both (14.4.10).

book_ref.quote: float in the air in the form of either solid particles or liquid droplets or both

blocks.prompt: 61 Which of the following is a man-made source of particulate matter?
blocks.explanation: Man-made PM sources include combustion, vehicle emissions and tobacco smoke; the others are natural (14.4.10).

book_ref.quote: Natural sources include volcanoes, fires, dust storms, and aerosolized sea salt.

blocks.prompt: 62 The major sources of heavy-metal air pollutants are:
blocks.explanation: Metallurgy, battery waste and incineration are the major sources of Pb, Hg and Cd (14.4.11).

book_ref.quote: Metallurgy, battery waste and incineration are their major sources.

blocks.text: 14.5 Impact of human activities on the atmosphere

blocks.prompt: 63 Human activities affect the atmosphere primarily through:
blocks.explanation: Human impact on the atmosphere is primarily through burning fossil fuels and deforestation (14.5).

book_ref.quote: primarily through the burning fossil fuels and deforestation

blocks.text: 14.5.1 Impact of burning fossil fuels on the atmosphere

blocks.prompt: 64 The primary cause of current climate change is:
blocks.explanation: The burning of fossil fuels is the primary cause of current climate change (14.5.1).

book_ref.quote: The burning of fossil fuels is the primary cause of current climate change

blocks.text: 14.5.2 Impact of deforestation on the atmosphere

blocks.prompt: 65 Deforestation is:

options.text: burning of fossil fuels in vehicles
purposeful clearing or thinning of forests by humans

blocks.explanation: Deforestation is purposeful clearing or thinning of forests by humans (14.5.2).

book_ref.quote: Deforestation is purposeful cleaning or thinning of forests by humans.

blocks.prompt: 66 Deforestation adds to climate change mainly because forests:
blocks.explanation: Forests absorb GHGs like CO₂ and clean the air; removing them leaves more CO₂ in the air (14.5.2).

book_ref.quote: Forests absorb GHGs like CO₂ and clean air for us.

blocks.prompt: 67 Smog is a type of air pollution typically characterized by:

options.text: a rise in ozone in the stratosphere

blocks.explanation: Smog is air pollution characterized by a thick haze, mostly in urban areas (14.6.1).

book_ref.quote: Smog is a type of air pollution typically characterized by a thick haze.

blocks.prompt: 68 Classical (industrial) smog is also called London smog. It results mainly from high quantities of:
blocks.explanation: Sulphurous or industrial smog results from high quantities of SOₓ released into the air (14.6.1).

book_ref.quote: It is also called London smog.

blocks.prompt: 69 Sulphurous smog is also called:
blocks.explanation: Sulphurous or industrial smog is also called reducing smog or classical smog (14.6.1).

book_ref.quote: also called as “Reducing smog or Classical Smog”

blocks.prompt: 70 Photochemical smog is also known as:
blocks.explanation: Photochemical smog is called Los Angeles smog; industrial smog is London smog (14.6.1).

book_ref.quote: undergo photochemical reactions in the presence of sunlight

blocks.prompt: 71 PAN, formed in photochemical smog, stands for:
blocks.explanation: NOₓ, VOCs and unburned hydrocarbons react in sunlight to form secondary pollutants like ozone and peroxyacetyl nitrates (PAN) (14.6.1).

book_ref.quote: form secondary pollutants like ozone and peroxyacetyl nitrates (PAN)

blocks.prompt: 72 Photochemical smog is considered more dangerous because it can cause:

options.text: heart palpitations, pneumonia and even lung cancer

blocks.explanation: Photochemical smog can cause heart palpitations, pneumonia and even lung cancer (14.6.1).

book_ref.quote: This type of smog is considered more dangerous

blocks.prompt: 73 Rain is called acid rain when its pH is:
blocks.explanation: Book correction: rain is acid rain when its pH is below 5.6; clean rain is already slightly acidic (about 5.6) (14.6.2).

book_ref.quote: Acid rain looks, feels and tastes like clean rain.

blocks.prompt: 74 In acid rain formation, SO₃ reacts with water to form:
blocks.explanation: 2SO₂ + O₂ → 2SO₃, then SO₃(g) + H₂O(l) → H₂SO₄(aq) (14.6.2).

book_ref.quote: SO₂ from fossil fuels is oxidized to SO₃ which then reacts with water to form sulphuric acid.

blocks.prompt: 75 The correct balanced equation for formation of nitric and nitrous acids in acid rain is:
blocks.explanation: Book correction: it is nitrogen dioxide that gives the two acids: 2NO₂(g) + H₂O(ℓ) → HNO₃(aq) + HNO₂(aq) (14.6.2).

book_ref.quote: Nitrogen oxide reacts with water to produce nitric acid and nitrous acid.

blocks.prompt: 76 Acid rain can damage places far away from the source of SOₓ and NOₓ because:

options.text: acids are formed only at the source
acid rain falls only near factories
wind carries the acidic droplets to huge distances

blocks.explanation: Wind can carry the acidic droplets to huge distances before they return as acid rain, hail, snow or fog (14.6.2).

book_ref.quote: Wind can carry these acidic droplets to huge distance.

blocks.prompt: 77 The progressive warming of the earth's surface due to the blanketing effect of certain gases is called:
blocks.explanation: This is the definition of the greenhouse effect (14.7).

book_ref.quote: The progressive warming up of the earth’s surface due to blanketing effect of greenhouse gases

blocks.prompt: 78 Global warming refers to:

options.text: the long-term rise in the earth's average surface temperature
the daily heating of the earth by sunlight
the heat given out when ozone forms

blocks.explanation: Global warming is the long-term rise in the earth's average surface temperature due to human GHG emissions (14.7).

book_ref.quote: Global warming refers to the long-term rise in the Earth’s average surface temperature

blocks.prompt: 79 Carbon dioxide and water vapour in the atmosphere:

options.text: let short-wavelength solar radiation pass but hold back long-wavelength heat radiation from the earth

blocks.explanation: CO₂ and water vapour transmit short-wavelength solar radiation but send back the longer-wavelength heat radiation from the warmed earth (14.7).

book_ref.quote: transmit short wavelength solar radiations

blocks.prompt: 80 The greenhouse effect is based on the ability of certain gases to absorb:
blocks.explanation: The greenhouse effect is based on gases absorbing infrared radiation (14.7).

book_ref.quote: The greenhouse effect is a phenomenon which is based on the gases to absorb infra-red radiations.

blocks.prompt: 81 According to the chapter, as the concentration of CO₂ and other greenhouse gases rises:

options.text: more heat is absorbed and the global temperature rises more
the earth loses more heat at night

blocks.explanation: Higher the concentration of CO₂ and other gases, greater the absorption of thermal radiation and the rise in global temperature (14.7).

book_ref.quote: greater will be the absorption of thermal radiations

blocks.prompt: 82 Which oxide of nitrogen does the chapter say contributes to climate change?
blocks.explanation: The increased levels of N₂O (nitrous oxide) contribute to climate change (14.4.2).

book_ref.quote: The increased levels of N₂O contribute to climate change

blocks.prompt: 83 The Air Quality Index (AQI) is a measure of:

options.text: the concentrations of pollutants in the air at a location

blocks.explanation: AQI measures the concentrations of pollutants present in the air at a particular location (14.8).

book_ref.quote: AQI is a measure of the concentrations of pollutants present in the air at a particular location.

blocks.prompt: 84 An AQI value over 300 is considered:
blocks.explanation: An AQI over 300 is considered hazardous (14.8, Table 14.2).

book_ref.quote: An AQI over 300 is considered hazardous.

blocks.prompt: 85 Which group is under high risk when the AQI is hazardous?
blocks.explanation: Children under 18, adults over 65 and people with chronic heart and lung diseases are under high risk (14.8).

book_ref.quote: Children under 18, adult over 65, people with chronic heart, and lung diseases are under high-risk.

blocks.prompt: 86 Outdoor workers are at higher risk from poor air quality because of:
blocks.explanation: Outdoor workers are at higher risk because of prolonged exposure (14.8).

book_ref.quote: Outdoor workers are at higher risk because of the prolonged exposure.

blocks.prompt: 87 On the AQI scale (Table 14.2), a value of 135 falls in the level:
blocks.explanation: 101 to 150 is Unhealthy for Sensitive Groups, colour orange (Table 14.2).

book_ref.quote: Unhealthy for Sensitive Groups

blocks.prompt: 88 On the AQI scale, a reading of 250 is shown in which colour?
blocks.explanation: 201 to 300 is Very Unhealthy, colour purple (Table 14.2).

book_ref.quote: Table 14.2 AQI and level of health concern

blocks.prompt: 89 The colour used for the 'Hazardous' level (AQI 301 to 500) is:
blocks.explanation: 301 to 500 is Hazardous, colour maroon (Table 14.2).

book_ref.quote: Table 14.2 AQI and level of health concern

blocks.prompt: 90 Poor air quality can result when pollutants are trapped near the ground by:
blocks.explanation: A layer of warm air trapping pollutants near the ground can lead to poor air quality (meteorological conditions, 14.8.1).

book_ref.quote: A layer of warm air trapping pollutants near the ground can lead to poor air quality.

blocks.prompt: 91 Seasonal pollen concentration affecting air quality belongs to which factor?
blocks.explanation: Seasonal changes include heating/cooling of buildings and seasonal pollen concentration (14.8.1).

book_ref.quote: Seasonal pollen concentration can contribute to poor air quality.

blocks.prompt: 92 Wildfires and natural dust storms affect air quality under the factor:
blocks.explanation: Natural events: wildfires release smoke and PM; dust storms lower air quality (14.8.1).

book_ref.quote: Natural dust storms can significantly lower air quality.

blocks.text: 14.9 Link between air quality and human health

blocks.prompt: 93 The health impacts of poor air quality can be:
blocks.explanation: Poor air quality can have immediate and long-term health impacts (14.9).

book_ref.quote: Poor air quality can have immediate and long-term health impacts.

blocks.text: 14.9.1 Major air pollutants and their health effects

blocks.prompt: 94 Inhaling particulate matter can cause inflammation of the airways leading to:
blocks.explanation: Inhaled PM can cause inflammation and irritation of airways, leading to asthma and bronchitis (14.9.1).

book_ref.quote: Inhalation of these particulate matter (PM) can cause inflammation and irritation of airways

blocks.prompt: 95 Long-term exposure to NO₂ and SO₂ can increase the risk of:
blocks.explanation: Short-term exposure irritates the respiratory system; long-term exposure increases the risk of respiratory infection, asthma and bronchitis (14.9.1).

book_ref.quote: The short-term exposures of NO₂ and SO₂ can irritate the respiratory system

blocks.text: 14.10 Potential health risks associated with air pollution

blocks.prompt: 96 The health effects of air pollution depend on:

options.text: type and concentration of pollutants, duration of exposure and individual weakness
only the colour of the smoke
only the time of the day

blocks.explanation: Effects can be acute or chronic and vary with type and concentration of pollutants, duration of exposure and individual weakness (14.10).

book_ref.quote: The potential health effects can be acute or chronic

blocks.text: 14.10.1 Main health risks associated with air pollution

blocks.prompt: 97 Ozone, PM and NO₂ can trigger:
blocks.explanation: Ozone, PM and NO₂ can increase asthma symptoms and trigger asthma attacks (14.10.1).

book_ref.quote: can increase asthma symptoms and trigger asthma attack

blocks.prompt: 98 Particulate matter increases the risk of heart attack by causing:

options.text: inflammation, blood vessel damage and high blood pressure

blocks.explanation: PM can raise heart-attack risk by causing inflammation, blood vessel damage and high blood pressure (14.10.1).

book_ref.quote: Exposure to particular matters and other pollutants can increase the risk of heart attack

blocks.prompt: 99 Prolonged exposure to PM and carcinogenic compounds such as benzene can cause:
blocks.explanation: Prolonged exposure to PM and carcinogenic compounds (benzene) causes lung cancer (14.10.1).

book_ref.quote: carcinogenic compounds (benzene formation) cause lung cancer

blocks.prompt: 100 A reproductive and developmental effect of air pollution is:
blocks.explanation: Air pollution may affect fertility in men and women, and premature birth and developmental problems in children may occur (14.10.1).

book_ref.quote: Premature birth and developmental problems in children may occur.

blocks.text: 14.11 Methods and techniques to measure and monitor air quality

blocks.prompt: 101 The instrument used to monitor particulate matter such as dust, smoke, mist and fumes is the:
blocks.explanation: The nephelometer is used to measure AQI and monitor PM such as dust, smoke, mist and fumes (14.11).

book_ref.quote: The instrument used to measure air quality index (AQI) is nephelometer.

blocks.prompt: 102 A nephelometer (photometer) detects particles by measuring:

options.text: the total amount of light they scatter

blocks.explanation: A nephelometer detects particles by measuring the total amount of light they scatter (14.11).

book_ref.quote: detects particles by measuring the total amount of light they scatter

blocks.prompt: 103 A Continuous Emission Monitoring System (CEMS) is usually used to monitor pollutants at:
blocks.explanation: CEMS usually monitors CO, O₃, SO₂, NO₂, VOCs and PM at industrial sites (14.11.1).

book_ref.quote: can usually monitor gas like CO, O₃, SO₂, NO₂, VOCs and PM at industrial sites

blocks.prompt: 104 Measuring pollutants over large regional and global areas is done by:
blocks.explanation: Satellites with sensors (remote sensing) measure pollutants over large areas (14.11.1).

book_ref.quote: Satellites equipped with sensors can measure atmospheric pollutants over large areas

blocks.prompt: 105 Fixed stations in urban and industrial zones that measure pollutant levels in real time are called:
blocks.explanation: AQMS are fixed stations with sensors and analysers measuring pollutant levels in real time (14.11.1).

book_ref.quote: Fixed monitoring stations are equipped with various sensors and analyzers

blocks.text: 14.12 Experiments and data collection to test a hypothesis about air quality

blocks.prompt: 106 The first step in designing an experiment about air quality is to:
blocks.explanation: As a first step, a hypothesis is developed to design an experiment (14.12 i).

book_ref.quote: As a first step, a hypothesis is developed to design an experiment.

blocks.prompt: 107 To test whether PM 2.5 and NO₂ are higher in peak traffic hours, the sites selected for monitoring are:

options.text: busy road sites and residential areas

blocks.explanation: Busy road sites and residential areas are selected for monitoring (14.12 ii).

book_ref.quote: Busy roads sites and residential areas are selected for monitoring.

blocks.text: 14.13 Analyse data and interpret air quality

blocks.prompt: 108 The collected air-quality data is analysed in order to:

options.text: confirm whether the hypothesis is true or false
make a new hypothesis before collecting data

blocks.explanation: The collected data is analysed to confirm the truth or falseness of the hypothesis (14.13).

book_ref.quote: The collected data is analyzed to confirm the truth or falseness of the hypothesis.

blocks.text: 14.14 Strategies used to reduce air pollution

blocks.prompt: 109 In a catalytic convertor, NOₓ are:
blocks.explanation: In a catalytic convertor CO is oxidized to CO₂ and NOₓ are reduced to N₂ (14.14 i).

book_ref.quote: CO is oxidized to CO₂. NOₓ are reduced to N₂.

blocks.prompt: 110 In a catalytic convertor, unburnt hydrocarbons are converted into:
blocks.explanation: The unburnt hydrocarbon is converted to CO₂ and H₂O (14.14 i).

book_ref.quote: The unburnt hydrocarbon is converted to CO₂ and H₂O.

blocks.prompt: 111 The primary function of a diesel particulate filter (DPF) is to:

options.text: capture and store soot particles from exhaust gases

blocks.explanation: The DPF captures and stores soot particles from exhaust gases (14.14 ii).

book_ref.quote: The primary function of diesel particulate filter is to capture and store soot particles

blocks.prompt: 112 Catalysts used in selective catalytic reduction (SCR) include:
blocks.explanation: SCR uses catalysts such as TiO₂ and zeolites (14.14 iii).

book_ref.quote: using catalysts, such as TiO₂, zeolites, etc.

blocks.prompt: 113 Scrubbers remove pollutants such as SO₂ and PM from industrial exhaust gases by using:
blocks.explanation: Scrubbers use liquids (e.g. H₂O) to remove SO₂ and PM from industrial exhaust gases (14.14 iv).

book_ref.quote: Scrubbers use liquids (e.g. H₂O) to remove pollutants such as SO₂, PM

blocks.prompt: 114 How many technologies to control emission of air pollutants does the chapter actually describe?
blocks.explanation: The chapter describes four: catalytic convertor, DPF, SCR and scrubbers (14.14).

book_ref.quote: A variety of technologies is used to reduce air pollution and improve air quality.

blocks.prompt: 115 PEPA, a law to control air pollution in Pakistan, stands for:
blocks.explanation: PEPA is the Pakistan Environmental Protection Act 1997 (14.15.1).

book_ref.quote: Pakistan Environmental Protection Act (PEPA 1997)

blocks.prompt: 116 NEQS stands for:
blocks.explanation: NEQS stands for National Environmental Quality Standards (14.15.1).

book_ref.quote: National Environmental Quality Standard (NEQS)

blocks.prompt: 117 Under the vehicle emission standard, the cleaner fuels promoted are:
blocks.explanation: The vehicle emission standard promotes cleaner fuels such as CNG and LPG (14.15.2).

book_ref.quote: The promotion of cleaner fuels such as compressed natural gas (CNG), liquid petroleum gas (LPG)

blocks.prompt: 118 A specific smog control measure named in the chapter is:

options.text: restricting the burning of crop residues

blocks.explanation: Smog control measures include restricting burning of crop residues and using smog towers (14.15.2).

book_ref.quote: Restrictions the burning of crop residues, which is a major contributes to smog

blocks.prompt: 119 Reducing the permissible level of sulphur in diesel mainly cuts the emission of:
blocks.explanation: Low-sulphur diesel reduces sulphur, and SOₓ come from burning such fuels (14.15.2, 14.4.3).

book_ref.quote: Use of low-Sulphur Diesel Reduction of permissible level of sulphur in diesel.

blocks.prompt: 120 Developing green belts and parks in urban areas is part of:
blocks.explanation: Urban planning and green infrastructure: green belts and parks; reducing traffic congestion (14.15.2).

book_ref.quote: Development of green belts and parks in urban / areas to improve air quality.

blocks.prompt: 121 An economic issue caused by poor air quality is:

options.text: reduced worker productivity due to illness and absenteeism

blocks.explanation: Economic: reduced productivity, crop damage raising food prices, acid rain damage to infrastructure (14.16.1).

book_ref.quote: Poor air quality can reduce worker productivity due to illness and absenteeism.

blocks.prompt: 122 Forced migration of people from polluted areas, leading to social displacement, is a:
blocks.explanation: Severe pollution forcing migration and social displacement is listed as a social issue (14.16.2).

book_ref.quote: Severe air pollution can force people to migrate from the unhealthy polluted areas

blocks.prompt: 123 Effective management of air pollution needs international cooperation because:

options.text: each country's air stays inside it
air pollution is not confined to borders

blocks.explanation: Air pollution is not confined to borders, so effective management requires international cooperation (14.16.3).

book_ref.quote: Air pollution is not confined to borders and effective management requires international corporation.
